issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an instance method named swiftExperienceDescription() (and instruct calling it from the initializer), but the solution implements and calls a method named getExperienceDescription() instead. This name/signature mismatch across artifacts is structural: students following the template/problem will implement swiftExperienceDescription(), while the solution uses a different identifier. This inconsistency can confuse students about the required method name and where it should be invoked and makes cross-checking against the provided solution misleading.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name and its use across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription() and update the initializer to call swiftExperienceDescription(), or (B) update the problem statement and template to require/getExperienceDescription() instead of swiftExperienceDescription(). Ensure the same method name (swiftExperienceDescription) is used in the specification, template stub, and reference solution.

issues.description: The developer description method is named inconsistently across artifacts. The Problem Statement and the Template define the method as swiftExperienceDescription(), but the Solution implements it as getExperienceDescription(). Additionally, the Solution's Client still calls swiftExperienceDescription(), creating a mismatch within the Solution itself. This breaks the one-to-one mapping of the required API and will confuse students about which method to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Rename the Solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription(), and update all calls to use swiftExperienceDescription(). This will align the Solution with the Problem Statement and Template and remove the internal Solution mismatch.
